input.title: Another History of Abortion. Contraception, Rights, and Health in Republican Italy
input.description:
As part of the lecture series "I Lunedì della Storia", curated by Matteo Di Tullio and Francesco Torchiani, the third meeting will take place featuring the book *Another History of Abortion. Contraception, Rights, and Health in Republican Italy* (Il Mulino 2026) by independent researcher Azzurra Tafuro. She will discuss the volume with Francesco Torchiani from the University of Pavia.

The book reconstructs the Italian history of contraception and abortion within a framework that deliberately transcends national borders. The decisive word is right there in the title: "another". Another history means first of all changing the point of observation. Instead of looking only at institutions, parties, and parliamentary chambers, it seeks out what was happening beneath the surface of official history. Azzurra Tafuro takes the reader into Cold War Italy and Europe, when abortion and contraception were at the center of a game involving population control—the so-called "demographic bomb"—biopolitics, reproductive and sexual health, and individual freedom all at once.

"It is also a history made of crossings," the author explains. "Borders in the book are not just lines drawn on maps. They are obstacles to circumvent. They are *poros* places, constantly traversed by information, people, practices, and possibilities."

Azzurra Tafuro's research indeed places Italy within a dense network of transnational relations and restores a central role to feminisms, birth control associations, the press, and the networks that allowed many women to seek elsewhere what was not yet obtainable in Italy.

Her previous scientific production includes precisely studies on the transnational networks of women's health and the international pathways through which Italian women sought access to abortion between the sixties and eighties. History then changes its face.

"It is no longer just the history of the laws that legalized abortion and contraception," the author emphasizes, "but the history of an epochal change that transformed what were crimes and private shames into forms of the right to health and self-determination. It is the history of those who fought for a private issue to become a public issue. It is the history of associations and movements that transformed reproductive health from an individual or even clandestine fact into a matter of rights. And it is also the history of resistances, fears, and conflicts that accompanied that process."

Azzurra Tafuro is a historian of the contemporary era, focusing on the political, cultural, and gender history of modern and contemporary Europe. Her research on abortion and contraception in Italy during the Cold War stems from an explicitly transnational approach and the perspective of history from below, attentive to the experiences and voices that remain at the margins of institutional narratives. It is a perspective particularly interesting for a meeting included in a series dedicated to history, because abortion does not belong solely to the history of women, nor solely to the history of medicine or law. It belongs to the history of power, the state and its relations with private life, family, sexuality, demography, social movements, and above all, the deep transformation of the very idea of citizenship.

input.title: Chernobyl: the catastrophe of Soviet «rationality»
input.description:
As part of the lecture series "Chernobyl 1986-2026. A disaster and its legacies", **Giuseppe Ghini**, full professor of Slavistics at the University of Urbino Carlo Bo, will address the topic *Chernobyl: the catastrophe of Soviet «rationality»*. 

The title *Chernobyl: the catastrophe of Soviet «rationality»* already contains a contradiction. Chernobyl was not simply the failure of a technology. It was also the crisis of a system that had built extraordinary confidence in its own ability to organize the world according to rational criteria. The Soviet Union was, at least in its self-representation, the country of planning and science at the service of the State, capable of mobilizing resources and men to achieve goals defined from above. Yet, within this system, a catastrophe was produced that laid bare its vulnerability: technical problems, operator errors, deficiencies in safety culture, and above all, an information management marked by delays and reticence.

The question, therefore, is not merely technical. It is political, social, and cultural. A society could build a nuclear apparatus and simultaneously prove incapable of managing information about what was happening inside a reactor. This is the contradiction that makes Chernobyl one of the great metaphors of the end of the twentieth century: a machine designed to master matter found itself facing something it could not master; the system that should have governed the emergency sought to govern the news of the emergency.

«The accident occurred in mature Soviet Union, a stable order, consolidated during the Brezhnev era and founded on an implicit pact between State and citizen. The State guaranteed work, social security, education, and health assistance. In return, it demanded obedience, conformity, and dependence on the organization. Transmitting bad news upward could mean being considered responsible for it; executing an organization's decision instead exposed one to lesser personal risk. Chernobyl – Professor Ghini explains – showed the consequences of this mechanism. Unwelcome information tended to be toned down at every hierarchical step, while reality was reduced to the categories foreseen by the apparatus. Even the destruction of the reactor initially appeared inconceivable, because the technical and administrative system had established that such an event could not happen. Soviet ideocracy did not limit itself to controlling decisions and public communication: it claimed to establish what was real and what meaning should be attributed to experience.»

«Here the contradiction of Gorbachev's *glasnost* emerged. Gorbachev had introduced the need for transparency into a system still founded on the political monopoly of the CPSU and on the control of information. Chernobyl revealed the structural limits of an order still capable of commanding and mobilizing, but incapable of learning from reality. The catastrophe thus called into question both the pact between State and citizen and the regime's claim to establish what citizens could know.»

The meeting is recognized by the IUSS School of Pavia as an extra-curricular educational activity of the Ordinary Courses.

input.title: The Zanardelli "moment". Interdisciplinary reinterpretations on the bicentenary of his birth (1826-2026)
input.description:
The **Collegio Ghislieri** commemorates the figure of the patriot and politician **Giuseppe Zanardelli**, two hundred years after his birth, with a **conference** that enjoys the **High Patronage of the President of the Republic** and will be held on **Wednesday, October 28, 2026** in the Aula Goldoniana.

Speeches—entrusted to specialized historians of politics, law, and literature from various generations—will offer an interdisciplinary reinterpretation of Zanardelli's figure beyond occasional celebration and will allow for the discovery or rediscovery of lesser-known aspects of the life and long career of the man, the statesman, and the media personality. They will propose contexts and perspectives capable of restoring the politicization of the young Ghislieri alumnus in the volcanic year 1848, his beginnings on the Lombard and national political scene, his networks, ministerial experiences, and media fortune, in life and posthumously, through his iconization in print as a celebrity of the time, but also as a literary character. Not Zanardelli "on a pedestal", then, but Zanardelli in the various seasons of his life, immersed in the experiences of the generation that discovered politics in clandestinity and volunteer service in arms in broad daylight, and that knew how to make a profession of politics, committing itself to the construction of the country, even coming to know in person its most distant peripheries. Such as Basilicata visited in an epic and rocambolesco journey in September 1902.

**Giuseppe Zanardelli (1826 - 1903)** is a prominent figure of the Risorgimento and the Historical Left and its values of freedom, progress, and social justice. The firstborn of a well-to-do bourgeois family from Brescia, in 1844 he enrolled in the political-legal faculty of the University of Pavia as an Alumnus of the Collegio Ghislieri. In 1848 **he participated in the Ten Days of Brescia** and was an exile in Switzerland after the defeat of the Piedmontese at Novara. In 1860 he began an impassioned adventure in the representative institutions of the new Kingdom. Initially a deputy of the Left, he was Minister of Public Works, of the Interior, of Justice, and President of the Chamber of Deputies. In 1889 he prepared the penal code that took his name and remained in force until the promulgation of the Rocco code (1930). He was Prime Minister from 1901 to 1903. His government inaugurated that liberal turning point that would characterize the first decade of the century. Political militancy never distanced Zanardelli from cultural commitment: he collaborated with Gaetano Semenza, in 1865, in the creation of the political-economic daily *Il Sole*, wrote for the democratic-republican periodical *La Voce del Popolo*, the newspaper *La Costituente italiana*, and the political propaganda periodical *Crepuscolo*.

cases.notes: Commemorative multi-speaker conference; the bicentenary does not make it a ceremony

input.title: Train for the Future: Female Sports Champions on Discipline, Teamwork, and Resilience - "Team up to win. Group, leadership, and individual contribution"
input.description:
What do the journeys of a university student and an athlete have in common? The ability to set long-term goals, train discipline and consistency, manage pressure and expectations, measure oneself against one's limits, and find the strength to start over after a setback. Both also teach the value of teamwork, individual responsibility, and the ability to find one's place within a community.

It is from this consideration that the **Collegio Nuovo** is hosting the lecture series **"Train for the Future – Female Sports Champions on Discipline, Teamwork, and Resilience"**, bringing together the experiences of high-level female athletes who also had their early sporting experiences in Pavia, alongside the growth path of university students.

**"Team up to win. Group, leadership, and individual contribution"** is the title of the first public event, scheduled at the Nuovo on **October 26, 2026** (**21:00**), featuring volleyball player **Alessia Gennari**, athlete of the Italian National Team and 2021 European Champion, who played for Riso Scotti Pavia in 2011-12. The event is moderated by **Cesare Zizza**, Pro-Rector for Persons and Student Welfare at the University of Pavia.

«We teamed up at the Nuovo in multiple senses and times – declares Rector **Grazia Bruttocao** – first, thanks to our student-athletes who with tenacity also this year (and for the thirteenth time!) managed to win the University Colleges Trophy promoted by CUS Pavia and the University of Pavia; then, we teamed up with one of them, Alessia Reale, a medical student and promoter of the *Women on Cleats* project who proposed this series to highlight the closeness between the life of an athlete and that of a student; finally, full harmony of intent with the University of Pavia, represented by Pro-Rector for Persons and Student Welfare Cesare Zizza and the delegate for Physical Wellness and Sport Cristina Montomoli, who will moderate the meetings.»

«Sport is neither male nor female – specifies **Cesare Zizza** – It is talent, commitment, passion, and the freedom to choose who we want to be. Yet, even today, stereotypes and prejudices condition the opportunities and aspirations, especially of young women. Overcoming them means building a freer, more inclusive sports culture respectful of everyone's abilities. I therefore warmly welcomed the invitation of Collegio Nuovo to participate in this initiative, which offers our students the opportunity to engage with experiences capable of inspiring, encouraging, and breaking down cultural barriers. Because sport, even before teaching how to win, teaches how to grow, to recognize the value of others, and to believe in one's own possibilities.»

The meeting with volleyball player Alessia Gennari, an athlete in a team sport, makes it possible to emphasize that the individual result, however excellent, is never separable from the functioning of the team. A way to address the concrete theme of collaboration, responsibility, and "silent leadership," in a context of strong and very diverse personalities: «The connection with the personal and formative growth of students is immediate – observes **Alessia Reale**, who is also a student at the IUSS School of Advanced Studies – learning to excel individually without losing the ability to build something together with others».

The second meeting, scheduled for **November 4** (21:00), features **Rebecca Nicoli**, Italian boxer (making her debut in Pavia) and Tokyo 2020 Olympian, who with **"Stepping into the ring: goals, falls, and restarts"** tackles another theme very close to students' hearts: in building a growth path, there is not only the moment of success, but also, as Nicoli's own story testifies, that of injury, setbacks, and the need to start over. Far from the stereotype of boxing as pure aggression, the tale of sport in the ring will also highlight the value of preparation, observation of the opponent, listening, and continuous learning, showing how resilience is built both inside and outside competition.

«Sport and physical activity represent fundamental tools for promoting health and well-being, not only physically, but also psychologically and socially. – declares **Cristina Montomoli**, delegate for Physical Wellness and Sport – For women, in particular, practicing physical activity means investing in one's health throughout life, strengthening self-confidence, developing autonomy and the ability to cope with difficulties. Meeting athletes who have been able to transform commitment, sacrifices, and difficult moments into growth opportunities offers our students an important occasion for reflection. The message we wish to convey is that sport should not be considered merely as competition or the pursuit of results, but as an integral part of a healthy lifestyle and a personal growth path accessible to everyone.»

With "Train for the Future," a program featuring two other appointments, the Collegio Nuovo renews its commitment to university education that pairs unavoidable academic preparation with the development of personal and relational skills: from the ability to collaborate and take responsibility to managing difficulties, from leadership to confidence in one's own possibilities. Learning to "win," in sport as in study, also means knowing how to face challenges, recognize the value of others, and find the strength to start over: it applies to everyone, men and women.

How to participate

Participation is free upon registration by:

- **October 25** for the meeting with Alessia Gennari ([registration link for the October 26 meeting](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfXOtN86wPI0xnuLncXs-6DzCjvBVkY0DjmQaI16zoP0edXpg/viewform?pli=1))

input.title: Mitochondria: more heat than light
input.description:
Academic lecture as part of the Honours Programme

Until recently it was assumed that mitochondria in mammalian cells operated at approximately the standard body temperature of 37 degrees Celsius. However, our recent data using different types of fluorescent reporter indicates a mitochondrial temperature of 50 degrees or above. In this lecture I shall present the evidence for this finding, the possible counter-arguments, and the consequences of elevated mitochondrial temperature for cellular and organismal physiology.

## About the lecturer

Howy Jacobs

Prof. Howard Jacobs has been a Professor of Molecular Biology at the University of Tampere from 1996 to 2023. His research interests include mitochondria, mitochondrial disease and cellular energy metabolism. Howy received the EU Descartes Prize for outstanding trans-national research in 2004 and has been chief editor of EMBO reports from 2009-2014. Since 2023, he is professor emeritus at the Tampere University.

input.title: Problematic Objects of Property – Form, Materiality, Politics
input.description:
Annual Conference of the Collaborative Research Center Structural Change of Property

In contemporary societies, we witness an ongoing extension of property regimes to data, cultural knowledge, human reproductive capacities, rivers, plant varieties, ecosystem services, academic teaching materials, and research results. At the same time, long-standing objects of property, such as land and housing, have been turned into chains of financial titles, such as debts and shares, that are linked to new modes of profiting and of everyday practice. In each case, the objects of property are newly delineated, transformed, and linked in favor of certain rights of use, exclusion, and income streams; they are also subjected to different forms of care or neglect. In this conference, we take the specificity of objects as a vantage point for understanding contemporary property relations. The world is not a passive material that can be transferred seamlessly into different forms of property. The (potential) objects of property follow a logic of their own that shapes the possible forms of owning them. While nearly everything can potentially become property, the peculiar materiality of things might also defy propertization. By focusing on the “problematic objects” of property, we envisage the processes of coding and re-coding property, the limits of property regimes, as well as their contestations. Our discussions are structured by these aspects:

**Formatting and Re-Coding**

What are the types of objectification that create the possibility to commodify, financialize or make common use of given or novel objects of property? How are different types of objectification linked to each other, transformed, and combined in order to fit different logics of exclusion or inclusion, control or autonomy, profitability and use?

**Material Limits of Property**

How does the materiality of property objects support or challenge their specific property status? How is the materiality of property objects linked to normative accounts of the limits of property? What material properties are foregrounded or ignored in the reconfiguration and creation of property?

**Politics of Propertization**

The coding and formatting of property objects is part of processes such as financialization, digitalization, ecological transformation, the reorganization of social reproduction and public infrastructures, and it is linked to contested divisions between public and private, distributions of use and gain, and access and exclusion. Counter-movements such as municipalization, cooperative production, and ecological conversion aim to re-format property objects and mobilize their material affordances against established property regimes. How is the materiality of the objects of property at stake in the politics of propertization and re- or de-propertization?

input.title: Networking for female Researchers – Building Competence, Strengthening the Community
input.description:
Workshop series for women* in the early stages of their academic careers

Networking Hands

Networking is considered to be one of the key skills for gaining visibility and moving forward in academia – and yet many female researchers find it difficult. All too often, networking comes across as artificial, strategic or simply time-consuming. In most cases, it is not a lack of willingness that is the problem, but a lack of practical tools – and the confidence that networking can be done authentically.

This is precisely where the ‘Networking for Female Researchers’ workshop series comes in: with practical exercises that address the challenges within the academic system and specifically strengthen the participants’ networking skills. At the same time, the series provides a space for exchange, mutual support and making new contacts. The aim is to promote networking, support the development of individual skills and help to boost self-efficacy.

The workshop series is aimed at women, trans*, inter*, non-binary and agender people who are currently undertaking postgraduate research. The workshops can be attended as a series, but it is also possible to take part in individual sessions.

The series is organised in collaboration with the Jena-based [TOP7 Network for Female Empowerment External link](https://topsieben.net/TOP7-NETZWERK). The three founders of the network will structure and host the workshops:

- Annelie Gallon (Lawyer for AI Law & Innovation)
- Eva-Maria Hartwich (Organisational development consultant I Co-Leadership-Coach)
- Marie Legrand (Digitalisation Officer at JenaKultur | Digitalisation & Transformation | IT Management)

The language of the workshops will be German. Childcare is available on request at both evening events.

## Part 1: ‘Networking with Attitude – Visible, Connected, Bold’

21 April, 18.00h – 21.00h, Auditorium Haus "Zur Rosen" (Johannisstr. 13)

In the first workshop, we invite you to reframe networking as a valuable resource. A role model talk with authentic insights into personal networking journeys, along with practical introductory exercises, will help you identify your own attitudes and experiment with initial tools. A moderated networking session will allow participants to build peer connections. The aim is to openly explore the conflicting relationship between competition and cooperation in academia, break down barriers, and encourage participants to invest their time and energy purposefully in networking.

## Part 2: “Developing networking skills – staying visible and making an impact”

5 November, 14.00h – 19.00h, Auditorium Haus "Zur Rosen" (Johannisstr. 13)

In the second workshop, we focus specifically on developing networking skills through pitch and self-presentation training. This strengthens the participants ability to introduce themselves in professional, interdisciplinary and informal contexts.

In a rotating speed-coaching format, the participants also receive personalised guidance on visibility, relationship-building and strategic career paths. A peer-learning exchange helps to collectively identify success factors and stumbling blocks.

The workshop concludes with the development of a personal networking strategy and the identification of concrete next steps. Participants therefore leave the workshop with a clear plan for their future networking. During and after the workshop, drinks and light refreshments provide an opportunity to strike up conversations with each other.

input.title: From Lab to Academia
input.description:
Evening talk on personal career paths in the natural and life sciences

The way from the laboratory to the doctorate

In the natural and life sciences, the lab is often where it all begins. Laboratory work is an integral part of many students’ academic training. From there, different paths can unfold: some graduates move into industry or other professional fields, while others continue on an academic path — pursuing a PhD, habilitation and eventually a professorship. And even then, Lab and Academia are not an either-or: professors may still spend time working in the lab alongside teaching, supervising and leading research.

“From Lab to Academia” describes one possible and often familiar trajectory — and the personal stories behind it. In our Career Talk, five scientists from different disciplines of the natural and life sciences will share insights into their individual careers and experiences along the way.

We’ll talk about PhDs and professorships, publications, networking, international experiences, work-life balance, mental health, science communication and AI in research — as well as the challenges, doubts and decisions that can shape an academic career.

On the podium will be:

## Readings – Books in Conversation

On Monday, October 26, at 6:00 PM, East European historian Prof. Dr. Martin Schulze Wessel (LMU Munich) will present his new book "Why Russia Will Not Stop. Seven Theses" at the Thuringian University and State Library Jena and discuss it with moderators Dr. Astrid Urban (ThULB) and Dr. Helmut Hühn (Schiller's Garden House) as well as the audience. Dr. Andreas Klinger, Director of the Thuringian University and State Library Jena, will give a welcoming address to open the new [event series](https://www.gartenhaus.uni-jena.de/902/lektueren) by the library and Schiller's Garden House.

## Martin Schulze Wessel: "Why Russia Will Not Stop. Seven Theses" (C.H.Beck)

Since Putin ordered the invasion of Ukraine, more than four years have passed. The war is already lasting longer than the entire First World War. Russian losses are high, and the economic costs are as well. Vladimir Putin could have ended the war at any time. Why hasn't he done so? Why does Russia keep fighting? And how realistic is the belief that Russia would keep the peace if a ceasefire were reached?

Martin Schulze Wessel analyzes the history of the Russian empire, explains why Russia's expansionist policy feeds on an imperial history, and shows what means have helped against Russian imperialism in the past. So far, the debate on Europe's security has been dominated primarily by political scientists and military experts. This book offers the perspective of historical science, without which Russia's motives cannot be understood.

"The seven theses of this book introduce the central fields of the imperial complex: territorial expansion, geopolitical hegemony, and imperial ideology. This complex is not an unalterable given in Russian history and present." (p. 13)

## Ramona Jesús: ›Zwei Quadratmeter Haut | Dos metros cuadrados de piel‹. With an afterword by Daniela Danz (Wallstein Verlag)

Cover "Zwei Quadratmeter Haut"

The voice that speaks to us readers in the poems of this volume is a multi-layered one, or in other words: it is composed of several voices.

We encounter the voice that reflects on writing, the voice that explores the aesthetics of passion, the voice that engages with art, painting, music, and other books, the voice that deals with economics, and last but not least, the voice of love. The poems address their time directly and critically, penetrating the narratives of a fragmented reality with the power of sensual insight. In doing so, they formally draw on elements and text types of popular culture, from the letter to the bank statement. Reading this debut volume reminds us that courage is the most important quality of a poetic voice.

"Two square meters of skin: The title has the sobriety of a survey and the imposition of a disclosure. [...] Our skin is our boundary to the outside and at the same time our largest receptive organ, memory, and alarm. Heat, shame, age, desire, injury show on it. Beneath it, things continue to work that should have long passed and been forgotten. In this book, skin is an archive. Memories, scars, history, and identity are inscribed into it [...]

At the beginning stands a poem 'that survives the destruction of this house'. That is a high stake". (Daniela Danz: On the poems of Ramona de Jesús)

input.title: Bodies before Words
input.description:
Medical Interventions in Children with Variations of Sex Characteristics

Questions surrounding medical interventions in children without capacity to consent—especially, though not exclusively, those born with variations of sex characteristics (VSC)—are increasingly examined through legal, ethical, medical, psychological, and social‑scientific lenses. Core claims advanced by intersex communities address two intertwined dimensions: protection and recognition. Public debate has often centered on civil‑status recognition under the banner of a “third option,” while protection calls for non‑pathologizing ethical and clinical standards and robust safeguards against sex‑characteristic‑modifying (“normalizing”) interventions on children who cannot consent, in order to preserve their independent development and an open future.

Narratives of urgency have long legitimized “normalizing” surgeries, yet these procedures are typically irreversible and may entail serious, long‑term physical and psychological harm. Recent scholarship and activism foreground childhood as a vulnerable yet highly individual phase, treating children as both beings and becomings, and advocating for temporal restraint until children can decide for themselves, alongside independent, expert, multidisciplinary counseling and support for children and parents.

This conference provides a platform for sustained, genuinely interdisciplinary exchange across philosophy/ethics, law, medicine, psychology, and the social sciences, adopting a participatory, community‑engaged approach that recognizes lived experience as indispensable knowledge and asks how best to realize these commitments in practice.

input.title: Doctoral Defense (Information and Communication Technology): MSc Sahar Salimpourkasebi
input.description:
MSc Sahar Salimpourkasebi will publicly present her doctoral dissertation “Deep learning for Robust Multi-Robot Perception and Control” for examination at the University of Turku on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at 12:00 PM (University of Turku, TIERS Lab, Tieronkatu 8, Turku).

The opponent is Doctor **Matti Kutila** (VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland Ltd) and the custos is Assistant Professor **Widhi Atman** (University of Turku). The event is held in English. The field of the dissertation is information and communication technology.

## Summary of the doctoral research:

Robots are increasingly expected to work alongside people and other robots in everyday environments. To do this reliably, they need to understand their surroundings, recognise misleading information, and move appropriately when conditions change. My dissertation investigates how artificial intelligence and sensor measurements can help robots meet these challenges. It brings together methods for determining where robots are, assessing the information they share, and learning how to move and respond to human guidance.

The first part of the research focuses on detecting unreliable information and building trust between robots. By comparing distance measurements, robots can identify sources of faulty information and improve their estimates of where they are relative to one another. Unreliable information can also come from other sensors, including cameras. The research shows how camera images can help robots detect new objects or changes in their surroundings without retraining the artificial intelligence models for every location. Comparing images collected by different robots also helps identify a robot that may be sharing misleading observations. A shared set of rules allows the team to distribute responsibility for deciding which information to trust.

The second part examines how robots can learn to move under different forms of guidance. In a “follow-me” setting, robots learn from examples to follow a leader accurately and smoothly using distance and direction measurements. The research also demonstrates how people can give robots commands through body postures recognised by small wearable sensors. For movement without direct human guidance, robots learn to navigate and avoid obstacles through practice in a computer simulation. Experiments show that this learning can be transferred to physical robots without retraining their movement models in the real world, although moving obstacles remain more challenging.

Together, these findings provide building blocks for more reliable robots that cooperate with one another and respond to people. Potential applications include inspecting buildings and industrial sites, transporting goods, and supporting people with mobility. By helping robots recognise unreliable information and learn useful movement skills, the research supports their wider use in everyday environments.

In UTU Career Services' English-language Multicultural Work-Life coaching, domestic and international university students reflect together on working life, their own identity, and cultural awareness from a career perspective. The goal is to understand how one's background, values, and interaction style influence professional development and collaboration with people from different cultures.

input.title: Two Hairy Tales – Puppet Theatre and Science Workshops for Children and Adults
input.description:
Workshops combining puppet theatre and nature research are organized in Turku from October to December. The stories and content are suitable for both adults and children (age limit 5 years).

The duration of the workshops is about 1 hour, and all workshop materials are available in Finnish and English.

## In the workshop, we experience puppet theatre and get to know urban nature

The first part of the workshops consists of two plays featuring two puppet theatre artists.

- The first play brings the famous fairy tale *Little Red Riding Hood* into the modern day. Follow Hood's story as she walks to her grandmother's house and encounters a wolf along the way. This time, however, the story has a new twist: the wolf might not be as bad as we are used to thinking...
- The second play tells the story of a poor young hare who has fallen into a trap. As if the situation weren't bad enough already, a singing fox arrives and notices him... but could this encounter truly be unsuccessful, or might it ultimately be the best thing that could happen to the hare?

After the plays, two activity desks will be available for children at the workshop. At the first desk, children can draw and share their feelings about the plays, and at the second desk, children can explore the puppets and meet the puppet theatre artists.

After the plays, research information on urban nature will also be on display at the workshop. Informative posters about the ecosystem services provided by urban forests, coexistence with predators, and opportunities to discuss with researchers will be available.

The planned duration of the workshops is a total of about 1 hour, after which discussions can optionally continue with the research team. Participants can also leave the workshop at any time (for example, right after the plays).

Light refreshments such as coffee, tea, fruit juices, and water will also be available. The workshops are completely free of charge.

## Why are the workshops organized?

Citizen participation significantly promotes sustainable nature conservation and long-term coexistence with nature. Environmental art has proven to be a particularly effective tool for promoting nature conservation for both children and adults.

Art can help clarify conflicts and deepen understanding by arousing interest and emotions regarding the topic while keeping the experience pleasant and inclusive.

For this reason, the Urban biophilia research group from the Department of Biology at the University of Turku is organizing open workshops in Turku that combine puppet theatre and science communication.

The goal is to share general knowledge about the ecology of urban forests and predators, dismantle irrational fears associated with these animals, show that predator predation is a natural and value-neutral phenomenon, and encourage the appreciation of urban forests as important places for connection with nature and recreation.

input.title: Jews of Coimbra
input.description:
The Municipality of Coimbra inaugurated on July 2, 2021, the exhibition "JEWS OF COIMBRA | from tolerance to persecution | memories and materialities". Installed in the central wing of the Inquisition Building (Pátio da Inquisition, in Coimbra), in a space that belonged, until its extinction in 1821, to the former Court of the Holy Office of the Inquisition of Coimbra, it opens to the public for the first time and where old "scars" survive to remember that long and painful time.

The exhibition aims to rescue and rehabilitate the memory of the Jewish communities that inhabited the urban territory, helping to deepen the knowledge of a long history, with still imprecise contours, which includes some particularities that differentiate it and make it remarkable.

The oldest documentary references to the Old Jewish Quarter of Coimbra (documents from 1130 and 1139) identify an important community heritage – Synagogue, Ritual Baths of Purification, Cemetery, Butcher's Shop and Albergaria – which clearly reflects the antiquity and importance of the Coimbra commune, one of the largest in Portugal in the 14th century.

The exhibition includes content associated with the growth of intolerance and anti-Judaism in Coimbra society which resulted, following the publication of the Manueline Edict of Expulsion (December 5, 1496), in the prohibition of Judaism and the establishment of the Inquisition in Portugal, from 1536..

The program of the exhibition "JEWS OF COIMBRA | from tolerance to persecution | memories and materialities" includes an important collection of objects, provided by the Israelite Community of Lisbon and the National Museum of Machado de Castro, also integrating a large-format reproduction of the survey of the Court of the Inquisition of Coimbra, carried out in 1634 by Matheus do Couto, provided by Torre do Tombo.

On display in the central wing of the Inquisition Building | Pátio da Inquisição, the exhibition has free admission. It can be visited from Tuesday to Saturday, from 13:00 to 18:00. Closed on Sundays, Mondays and holidays.

Beginning in 2013, “Crochet Social” takes on a strong collaborative character, actively involving residents and merchants of Rua Fernandes Tomás, who contribute to the decoration of the public space through the gathering of materials and the installation of various pieces, such as bed blankets and patchwork quilts, doilies, and tablecloths.

The installation also contributes to the enhancement of local commerce by boosting the circulation of people during the months it remains exposed, until the end of November.

**Tool for inclusion**

The project highlights the value of handcrafted work as a tool for inclusion and combating social isolation, promoting encounters between generations and reinforcing the sense of community. Year after year, “Crochet Social” also asserts itself as an expression of the cultural identity of the street and the city of Coimbra, demonstrating how art can contribute to solidarity and the vitality of the urban space.

cases.notes: Street installation of crochet work against isolation of the elderly; 'Social' in the title is not a gathering

input.title: Traveling and Writing – Coimbra from the 16th to the 19th Century
input.description:
The exhibition “Traveling and Writing – Coimbra from the 16th to the 19th Century” opens at the Almedina Tower on Tuesday, July 21st. Built from the work of Carlos Xavier Reis and curated by him, the exhibition brings together visual and written records produced by foreign travelers who passed through Coimbra between the 16th and 19th centuries, revealing different perspectives on the city over the course of almost four centuries. The exhibition will be on display until May 22, 2027.

The Almedina Tower hosts, starting July 21st, the exhibition “Traveling and Writing – Coimbra from the 16th to the 19th Century”, which invites the public to discover how foreign travelers observed, described, and represented Coimbra between the 16th and 19th centuries. The opening is scheduled for 18:00 and will be attended by the Councilor for Culture of the Municipality of Coimbra, Margarida Mendes Silva, and curator Carlos Xavier Reis.

**A look at Coimbra through travelers**

Through drawings, engravings, lithographs, and watercolors, in dialogue with travel accounts, the exhibition reveals different perspectives on the city, its spaces, and its daily life. Many of these testimonies are part of the “Estampas Coimbrãs”, published by the Municipality of Coimbra in 1964, constituting an important documentary heritage for the preservation of Coimbra's memory and image.

In coordination with Carlos Xavier Reis's book, “The University of Coimbra and its Students in the Eyes of Foreign Travelers (1581-1879): 298 Years of Literary Fragments”, the exhibition proposes a reflection on how visitors constructed narratives about the city, establishing a parallel with current ways of recording and sharing travel experiences.

The exhibition can be visited until May 22, 2027, at the Almedina Tower, from Tuesday to Saturday, from 10:00 to 13:00 and from 14:00 to 18:00. The venue is closed on Sundays, Mondays, and holidays.

cases.notes: Exhibition of historical travellers' records; travel is the record's origin, not the subject; 'invites the public to discover' names the public

input.title: Exhibition: Mirrors - Inside and outside reality
input.description:
**Mirrors - Inside and outside reality** is the current **central exhibition** of the UC Exploratório - Centro Ciência Viva of the University of Coimbra, now open to the public, once again within the framework of the global collaboration agreement established with the "la Caixa" Foundation | BPI.

The exhibition *Mirrors - Inside and outside reality* invites visitors to explore the reality "inside" and "outside" these everyday objects, in a surprising proposal for all audiences that fascinatingly combines art, mathematics, and light.

**Inside the mirror: experimenting and understanding**

Like Alice, the visitor is invited to step through a mirror and discover what lies on the other side. The exhibition begins with an installation of distorting mirrors that challenges perception and questions the relationship between reality and image, highlighting the importance of doubt in scientific thought.

Throughout the journey, visitors can explore different types of mirrors—plane, curved, and kaleidoscopic—as well as understand fundamental concepts of light reflection.

The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence of a light ray is equal to the angle of reflection. In plane mirrors, the image is formed at a distance equal to that of the object, but with lateral inversion. When we combine several mirrors at different angles, surprising visual effects emerge that highlight mathematical and geometric relationships.

Geometry plays a central role here, with the creation of axes of symmetry that multiply the images. The smaller the angle between mirrors, the greater the number of generated images. In kaleidoscopes, this logic leads to almost infinite visual patterns, providing immersive experiences that explore visual perception.

Curved mirrors—concave and convex—introduce new properties, fundamental for optics and the creation of lenses. They allow for magnified or reduced images, with practical applications in daily life and various fields of science.

The exhibition also presents examples of anamorphoses, distorted images that can only be correctly interpreted from a specific viewpoint, a technique used throughout the history of art.

**Mirrors and light: scientific and technological applications**

On the other side of the mirror, we find light. Without it, we could not see the surrounding reality, nor would mirrors make sense. Light is composed of photons, which simultaneously behave as waves and particles when interacting with matter, transporting energy and information.

Thanks to mirrors, it is possible to control and direct light for various applications, such as heating, illuminating, measuring, navigating, or even exploring space. Some modules of the exhibition show how it is possible to guide light and take it to specific locations, recreating, for example, systems similar to those that may have been used to illuminate spaces without natural light. For example, it is possible to mimic the sun and bring its light to settlements located in dark valleys where it does not reach during the winter months. Some modules also invite us to experiment with different types of reflections.

---

**Mirrors and the arrival at the Moon**

Another application of mirrors to direct light is retroreflectors, systems capable of returning light exactly to its source, in the same direction but in the opposite sense. They are used, for example, as reflectors on bicycles or in reflective materials, allowing greater visibility in the dark.

Throughout history, humanity has sought to develop instruments that allow a better understanding of its place on Earth and the exploration of the universe. In this context, the astronauts of the *Apollo 11*, *Apollo 14*, and *Apollo 15* missions used retroreflectors to precisely measure the distance between the Earth and the Moon and analyze variations in their relative positions.

---

**Light hunters: telescopes**

The exhibition also highlights the role of telescopes, fundamental instruments for the exploration of space. Equipment such as the [Hubble](https://hubblesite.org/) or [James Webb](https://webb.nasa.gov/) telescope uses mirrors to capture light coming from very distant objects.

Since light takes time to travel, observing the universe is also looking into the past. The *James Webb* Space Telescope, the most advanced ever launched, allows for unprecedented images of the cosmos, opening a new era in astronomy.

---

**Invisible light**

Not all light is visible. Infrared radiation, for example, carries thermal energy and cannot be detected by the human eye. The exhibition includes experiments that allow visitors to understand this phenomenon and explore its applications in areas such as communication, industry, and health.

---

**Information:** 239 703 897 | [**visitas@exploratorio.pt**](mailto:visitas@exploratorio.pt)

cases.notes: Science centre exhibition 'for all audiences'; 'for all audiences' names the public

input.title: ARCA. Architectures of Rupture, Bodies and Absences
input.description:
The Coimbra Municipal Museum hosts, starting Saturday, September 5, the exhibition “ARCA. Architectures of Rupture, Bodies and Absences”, an international artistic proposal that seeks to make visible, through contemporary creation, the gender inequalities that persist in the Iberian Peninsula. The exhibition, with free admission, can be visited until November 22, at Edifício Chiado.

Directed and curated by Victoria Esgueva López and Susana García Rams, professors and researchers at the Universitat Politècnica de València, “ARCA” presents a set of unpublished works conceived specifically for the project, from an approach that crosses artistic creation, research, and social analysis.

The exhibition starts from a reflection on the absences, fractures, and structural inequalities that cross women's experience, taking as a starting point official data relating to different dimensions of daily life. Access to employment, presence in positions of responsibility, the wage gap, the distribution of domestic tasks, and responsibility for care are some of the realities addressed by the artists.

Official statistics, institutional reports, and data from international observatories in Spain and Portugal thus constitute the starting material for creation. Words and objective data are transformed into artistic matter, giving rise to images, spaces, and narratives that seek to challenge the public and promote reflection on realities that, despite being persistent, are often normalized or remain invisible.

**20 artists selected for the relevance of their careers**

The proposal brings together 20 artists selected for the relevance of their professional careers and for the relationship of their artistic and academic production with the themes under analysis: Amparo Berenguer Wieden, Victoria Esgueva, Chele Esteve, Amparo Galbis Juan, Susana García Rams, Begoña Jordá Albiñana, María Martín Gallego, Hortensia Mínguez García, Paula Santiago, Ana Tomás, Sara Vilar García, Inmaculada Carpe, Vanesa Valero, Célia Bragança, Regina Costa, Manuela Cristóvão, Sónia Rafael, Isabel Pyrrait, Inez Wijnhorst and Maria do Carmo Raminhas Mendes.

The works presented are unpublished paintings of homogeneous format, made specifically for “ARCA”. The set constructs a collective and critical reading of the differences between women and men, transforming information and evidence into visual experiences capable of arousing dialogue and social conscience.

The project continues the award-winning experience of “NA-INMENSO: The Word in Art”, although it assumes its own conceptual and formal identity. In “ARCA”, the word maintains a structuring role, but appears anchored in concrete data and confronted with social reality, establishing a relationship between research, statistics, and artistic creation.

The itinerary of “ARCA” begins at the Coimbra Municipal Museum, subsequently moving to different exhibition spaces in Spain. The course of the exhibition also aims to reinforce cultural exchange between Portugal and Spain, precisely the two territories that constitute the center of the analysis developed by the artists.

cases.notes: Art exhibition on gender inequality; 'Architectures' is a metaphor in the title

input.title: Café Curto 2026
input.description:
Every Tuesday at 19:30. Free admission, subject to venue capacity. The schedule is interrupted during the months of July and August.

Café Curto returns in 2026 to the Café Concerto of Convento São Francisco with an expanded program and a new phase of growth, also marking the 10th anniversary of this cultural facility. With weekly sessions between January and June and from September to December, the cycle reinforces its standing as a reference in the promotion of emerging music, introducing new curatorial axes, deepening partnerships, and increasing the involvement of the local and national artistic community. Curated by Blue House, co-produced by Convento São Francisco, and funded by the Coimbra City Council, the project consolidates a path initiated during the pandemic context that gave rise to sub-cycles such as Café Duplo, MIC – Música Independente de Coimbra, and Café Longo.

Among the main new features of 2026 are the partnership with the Emergente Festival, which will bring five dates dedicated to new talents selected through a national open call, and the reinforcement of work with the Jazz Professional Course of EACMC, through artistic residencies with public presentation. MIC will also include an intensive mentoring program involving educational entities in the city. Throughout the year, Café Curto also articulates with other cultural events in Coimbra and presents more than forty sessions, affirming itself as a space for encounter, experimentation, and artistic dialogue in the cultural context of the city.

Program

13.01 JOANA GUERRA + MIGUEL GOUVEIA

Joana Guerra (Lisbon, 1983) is a cellist, composer, and improviser, moving between experimental music, improvisation, noise, folk, and jazz. With a career marked by interdisciplinary collaboration in contexts of music, dance, performance, and theater, she develops a singular sonic universe, also expressed in her solo records, among which Chão Vermelho stands out, and in multiple collective projects of exploratory and improvised music.

Miguel Gouveia, born in Santo Tirso with roots in the Douro region, is an editor, translator, oral storyteller, and musician. Founder of Bruaá Editora, after a career in teaching and training in children's and youth literature, he has dedicated himself since 2008 to independent publishing, reading aloud, and literary mediation, currently serving as a bookseller at Bruaá / Livraria do Convento, in Coimbra.

20.01 MARTA LIMA

Singer-songwriter Marta Lima released her debut EP, Murmúrio, in 2023, establishing herself since then as one of the most promising voices in new Portuguese music. With an ascending career, she has performed on some of the country's main stages, opening concerts for Vitor Kley and Bárbara Tinoco, performing on the main stage of the Algarve Academic Week, and collaborating with names such as Buba Espinho, Samuel Úria, and Joana Alegre. She also features in the lineups of benchmark festivals such as Festival F, NOS Alive, and Vodafone Paredes de Coura.

In 2024 she released the singles Passos Marcados, with prominent airplay on Antena 1, Antena 3, and TSF, and in 2025 she presented her second EP, Postal em Branco, at a sold-out concert at Musicbox, followed by a national tour of over 25 dates. With intimate writing, a captivating stage presence, and growing recognition, Marta Lima consolidates her place in the new generation of author-driven music made in Portugal.

This showcase is curated by the Emergente Tour of the Emergente Festival.

27.01 JP SIMÕES + PEDRO RENATO

JP Simões is a singer, songwriter, lyricist, and playwright, with a career starting in 1995 and a path spanning projects such as Pop Dell’Arte, Belle Chase Hotel, Quinteto Tati, and solo releases. Winner of the 2019 SPA Authors Award for Alvoroço, he recently released JP Simões canta José Mário Branco (2024), reaffirming himself as one of the most consistent and singular voices in contemporary Portuguese music.

Pedro Renato is a musician and producer, known as one of the founders of Belle Chase Hotel, with a career marked by multiple projects on the Portuguese musical landscape, including Wraygunn, Mancines, and Azembla’s Quartet. He has also developed work creating soundtracks for cinema and has extensive activity as a music producer, collaborating with artists such as Legendary Tigerman, JP Simões, Belle Chase Hotel, and António Olaio.

03.02 PUÇANGA

Puçanga is a singer, songwriter, and music producer based in Portugal. The name Puçanga, which means spell or home remedy, translates an artistic identity where a strong, exploratory voice intersects with experimental electronics featuring dark and bassy tones. Inspired by folklore and songs of resistance, her music addresses themes such as social justice, feminism, and the electricity of emotions. She recently released the single Maldigo. Vera Marques, creator of the Puçanga project, develops work in the areas of music, multimedia, and art education.

10.02 SOPHIE DJEBEL ROSE

Franco-Moroccan artist Sophia Djebel Rose brings us singular and rare music, difficult to classify. Crossing folk, noise, experimental song, and avant-garde poetry, born into permanent exile between two countries, she transformed nomadism into her greatest strength. On stage, she performs solo, using only an electric guitar, giving voice to the beauty of the lands she left behind in a gesture of evocation and resistance. Her live performances intertwine Mediterranean sounds with ecological and feminist themes. Her most recent album, Sécheresse, released in February 2025, gathers nine hypnotic, genre-crossing tracks that are simultaneously austere and baroque, dark and luminous, raw and refined.

17.02 JHON DOUGLAS

Jhon Douglas is a musician, visual artist, and performer, born in Rondônia, in the Brazilian Amazon, and based in Lisbon since 2016. His work crosses music, performance, and visual arts, developing a distinct language between experimentalism and popular song. He has released the EP MATO (2019), the album Jhon Douglas JungleBoys & Maritacas (2022), and the EP Artista Chinelo (2024), affirming a path of constant reinvention, presented on major stages in Portugal, as well as in Brazil, the Netherlands, and Spain.

With references ranging from Tom Zé and Itamar Assumpção to the energy of Alceu Valença and Elis Regina, Jhon Douglas constructs a singular artistic universe. In parallel, he develops the Arapucagongon project, in collaboration with Henrique Silva, dedicated to researching and connecting soundscapes between Brazil and Cape Verde.

24.02 AFONSO CABRAL + CAIO

Afonso Cabral (Lisbon, 1986) has been a constant presence in Portuguese music over the last 15 years, whether with You Can’t Win, Charlie Brown, in collaborations with Bruno Pernadas, Minta & The Brook Trout, or Mais Alto!, or as a songwriter for other performers. In 2024 he released Demorar, his second solo album, widely praised by critics, succeeding Morada (2019), in a career marked by intimate writing and a singular voice at the center of the song.

CAIO is one of the most sensitive voices in contemporary Portuguese song. At 27 years old and with seven released albums, he presents Ritmo de Procura (2024), a work that celebrates the simplicity of emotions and the depth of human connections, affirming himself as a storyteller attentive to fragility, tenderness, and authenticity in an accelerated time.

03.03 CPJAZZ

Recognizing the crucial importance of early stages and live performances, students from the Jazz Instrumental Professional Course at the Artistic School of the Coimbra Conservatory of Music take to the Café-Concerto stage to showcase much of what they learn in the immersive world of their academic training. Their presence in Café Curto arises primarily as a challenge for the young musicians to present original repertoire and work. Throughout 2026, the Jazz Combo showcases will be intensively prepared during a residency/artistic internship at the Blue House studio.

10_03_JULIEN TASSIN

Julien Tassin is a Belgian guitarist with a singular approach. With original tunings and a raw, lyrical language, he fuses blues, jazz, classical, oriental, and oriental-inflected styles, creating intense soundscapes where freedom, emotion, and experimentation meet. Julien Tassin presents Wild Around (Challenge Records, December 2024), his fourth solo album. Inspired by the world's savagery and inner storms, the Belgian guitarist explores the rawness, lyricism, and freedom of his music, where blues, jazz, classical, and world influences intersect. Recorded with minimal post-production, each track is an intimate dance between musician and guitar, offering the listener an intense, textured, and deeply captivating journey.

17.03 LIBRA

Libra is a singer, rapper, and composer, fusing conscious hip-hop, alternative R&B, and experimental soul. Her debut album, Everyone’s First Breath, released in May 2026, asserts itself as a manifesto of feminine sensitivity and strength, revealing a mature and committed artistic identity. Recognized by critics and acclaimed by the public, Libra has been building a promising path. In 2025 she received the Music Honorable Mention at the FNAC New Talents and, together with the band Mão Cabeça, will represent Portugal in the GrassRoots European new talent contest.

24.03 MERAI

Mariana Frangioia Portela, born in 2000 in Lisbon, operates under the artistic name "Merai," inspired by a character she created, a bird-woman. She seeks to explore the fragmentation of the being, reflecting on the need for union. Therefore, her work encompasses diverse genres and deep themes, ranging from manifesto-songs against sexual violence to indiefolk melodies about love and ancient legends. She presents herself in a new stage format, featuring a band and performance.

31.03 MARGARIDA CAMPELO + WOLF MANHATTAN

Margarida Campelo is a prominent presence in Portuguese music, known for her collaborations with Bruno Pernadas, Cassete Pirata, Joana Espadinha, or Minta & The Brook Trout, as a keyboardist and singer. She debuted as a solo artist in 2023 with Supermarket Joy, an acclaimed album crossing pop, soul, R&B, and experimental jazz, and in 2025 she presented Eu Sei Que o Amor, a finalist entry for Festival da Canção, anticipating new works.

Wolf Manhattan is one of the projects of João Vieira, a DJ, musician, and producer whose career began in London in the late 1990s. A central figure in the Portuguese clubbing scene of the 2000s as DJ Kitten and founder of Club Kitten, he has released ten albums across his solo career and X-Wife. Since 2020 he has developed soundtracks for theater and cultural projects, and in 2023, he published The Story of Wolf, his first work of fiction.

07.04 MIC

Since 2022, Blue House has organized an Open Call integrated into the Café Curto Cycle program, aiming to provide a stage and support emerging artists in their early steps. In 2026, five projects will be selected through the MIC: Música Independente de Coimbra call, open to all artists born or residing in the Central Region, to perform on the Café Concerto stage of Convento São Francisco. A privileged space to discover and see some of the new names in emerging Portuguese music.

14.04 CPJAZZ

Recognizing the crucial importance of early stages and live performances, students from the Jazz Instrumental Professional Course at the Artistic School of the Coimbra Conservatory of Music take to the Café-Concerto stage to showcase much of what they learn in the immersive world of their academic training. Their presence in Café Curto arises primarily as a challenge for the young musicians to present original repertoire and work. Throughout 2026, the Jazz Combo showcases will be intensively prepared during a residency/artistic internship at the Blue House studio.

21.04 ESTEVES SEM METAFÍSICA

Esteves sem Metafísica was born Teresa in 1991 and grew up in Arruda dos Vinhos, where the landscape and silence became raw material for her writing and music. Graduated in Arts and Humanities from the Faculty of Letters of Lisbon, she began her creative journey between literary and music criticism, with occasional contributions to the magazine Brotéria since 2018. In 2023 she self-published her poetry book A Morte não tem Pátria, an exercise in lucidity and fearlessness marking the emergence of a singular voice in the contemporary Portuguese landscape.

At the end of 2024, she undertook an artistic residency in Cernache, where she composed two of the songs included in her debut album, de.bu.te., a work crossing word, sound, and texture in a gesture of liberation from excess, reconciliation with the everyday, and recognition of fragility as an unexpected source of strength. Inspired by Álvaro de Campos's character in Tabacaria, she adopts restlessness as a method and doubt as a starting point, within an imaginary shared by the Beatles, literature, Irish culture, and a secret love for Fado, combining melancholy, humor, intensity, and a stubborn curiosity for human imperfection.

28.04 BERNARDO MOREIRA + GIL DIONÍSIO

Bernardo Moreira is one of the most active and recognized double bass players in Portuguese jazz, with a career starting in 1985 in Moreiras Jazztet. Trained with masters such as Niels-Henning Ørsted Pedersen, Rufus Reid, and Reggie Workman, he develops an intense activity as a musician and educator, joining the faculty of the Lisbon School of Music. He has collaborated with a large share of national and international jazz musicians and regularly performs at benchmark festivals and stages in Portugal and abroad.

Gil Dionísio (1988) is a multidisciplinary artist crossing music, literature, performance, radio, cinema, and visual arts. Author of the book A Particularidade dos Bichos e Outras Animalidades (2021), he has developed extensive solo and collective musical work since 2011, moving between punk, traditional, noise, electronics, and vocal experimentation. Founder of Rádio Trauma and various cultural platforms, he is also a director, DJ, and curator, maintaining an artistic practice deeply tied to the word, the voice, and poetic-political intervention.

05.05 ESTEVES

Following his self-titled 2019 album and O Alpinista (2022), acclaimed by Blitz as one of the records of the year, Esteves — also lyricist and vocalist for Trêsporcento — returns in 2025 with the EP Onde Seria Onde. In O Alpinista, the musician tackled contemporary themes such as the refugee drama (Que o Mar Leve), the pandemic (Ter Onde Ficar), and the celebration of Portugal's natural beauty (Caminho Plano). In the new EP, featuring several guests including Cat Falcão (Golden Slumbers, Monday), Frankie Chavez, and Pedro Branco, Esteves deepens his exploration of the human condition and the social and cultural context shaping it, crossing traditional Portuguese folk with Anglo-Saxon folk, always guided by his unmistakable Portuguese writing. In this showcase, Esteves takes on vocals and guitars, accompanied on stage by multi-instrumentalist João Gil (Vitorino Voador, You Can't Win, Charlie Brown, SAL).

12.05 MIC

Since 2022, Blue House has organized an Open Call integrated into the Café Curto Cycle program, aiming to provide a stage and support emerging artists in their early steps. In 2026, five projects will be selected through the MIC: Música Independente de Coimbra call, open to all artists born or residing in the Central Region, to perform on the Café Concerto stage of Convento São Francisco. A privileged space to discover and see some of the new names in emerging Portuguese music.

19.05 LIKA

LIKA, born in Kazakhstan, graduated from the Tchaikovsky Almaty Music College and the Hot Club of Lisbon, residing in Portugal since 2015. Since then, she has won over audiences with her original songs, solo or accompanied by her band, performing in intimate venues like Teatro Bocage and larger stages like the Paredes de Coura Festival (Jazz na Relva).

A composer in Portuguese and English, singer, and guitarist, LIKA develops a musical language crossing rock, jazz, pop, and soul. She participated prominently in The Voice in 2021 and is currently recording a new album of originals in Portuguese and English, in collaboration with Luíz Caracol and João Cabeleira.

26.05 ESTELA ALEXANDRE + MARIA ROQUE

Born in Leiria, Estela Alexandre began her musical journey on the piano, passing through the Orfeão de Leiria, the Coimbra Conservatory of Music, and the Lisbon School of Music, where she graduated in Jazz, deepening orchestral composition. She works as a performer, composer, and arranger, collaborating with various musicians and jazz orchestras in Portugal and abroad, including the Basel Jazz Orchestra. Winner of the Leiria International Musical Composition Competition in 2023, she is also an educator, currently teaching at the School of Rock in Lisbon.

Maria Roque, born in Castelo Branco, began her musical journey in piano and voice, receiving classical training at the Regional Conservatory of Castelo Branco. In 2020 she launched her solo project MaZela, asserting the Portuguese-language song as a space of intimacy and transformation. Her debut EP, Desgostos em Canções de Colo (2024), was widely acclaimed, leading her to stages and festivals such as NOS Alive and Vodafone Paredes de Coura, and she is also part of Human Natures.

02.06 MAIA BALDUZ

"Maia Balduz in Duo" is a concert featuring songs written by Maia Balduz and Simão Bárcia, captured on their self-titled debut album, with a musical language influenced by jazz, pop, fado, and classical music. Maia and guitarist Simão Bárcia set various poems to music, most of which are taken from Fernando Pessoa's unpublished works ("Inéditos"), a body of work they felt important to highlight given its relative obscurity.

09.06 CAMAFEU

Eduardo Roque Martins dons the skin of a country haunted by nostalgia and gives voice to old tales, the kind heard around late hearths told by characters weathered by time and space. He brings an instrumental music project focused on classical and electric guitar, exploring resonances, phase shifting, and improvisation.

His debut record gave us a handful of galloping, stubborn harmonies. More recently, he released Ex-Voto, a work of a more spiritual nature focusing on the idea of faith, unfulfilled promises, and where it resides. This Camafeu always tells us where it has been and guides us through an impressionistic and intricately landscaped set.

16.06 CPJAZZ

Recognizing the crucial importance of early stages and live performances, students from the Jazz Instrumental Professional Course at the Artistic School of the Coimbra Conservatory of Music take to the Café-Concerto stage to showcase much of what they learn in the immersive world of their academic training. Their presence in Café Curto arises primarily as a challenge for the young musicians to present original repertoire and work. Throughout 2026, the Jazz Combo showcases will be intensively prepared during a residency/artistic internship at the Blue House studio.

23.06 MIC

Since 2022, Blue House has organized an Open Call integrated into the Café Curto Cycle program, aiming to provide a stage and support emerging artists in their early steps. In 2026, five projects will be selected through the MIC: Música Independente de Coimbra call, open to all artists born or residing in the Central Region, to perform on the Café Concerto stage of Convento São Francisco. A privileged space to discover and see some of the new names in emerging Portuguese music.

30.06 ANDRE JÚLIO TURQUESA

Four years after releasing Orgônio, considered by Blitz as one of the top 50 national albums of 2020, André Júlio Turquesa — singer-songwriter, composer, and multi-instrumentalist musician, also known for his theater and cinema soundtrack compositions — now presents his new COMPLAINTS BOOK (DISCO DE RECLAMAÇÕES).

An album composed of 11 tracks with his own music and lyrics, sung in Portuguese, featuring various national and international artists, blending Indie Folk, Traditional Portuguese, and World Music.

08.09 DELA MARMY

Dela Marmy performs her delicate and sensitive debut album Acaso live, the successor to the EPs Captured Fantasy and Dela Marmy. The showcase oscillates between density and lightness in gestures, words, singing, and dancing, starting from a poetic, raw, empathetic, and political body. In Acaso, composed of song-letters in Portuguese, the artist reflects on love, searching, loss, intimacy, disintegration, desire, and hope, highlighting the serendipity of life and the unexpected possibilities that open up. The album acts as a manifesto against superficiality, individualism, uncritical culture, the dictatorship of the algorithm, and detachment so prevalent in today's society.

15.09 SARA CRUZ

Sara Cruz is an Azorean singer-songwriter who has won over audiences and critics with her international and engaging sound. Born in the middle of the Atlantic, between Europe and North America, she incorporates the influence of folk, blues, and R&B into her work, mixed with the pop/singer-songwriter universe. Recognized as a FNAC New Talent (2019), winner of NiT New Talent (2019), she participated in the House of Talents documentary (2021) and was selected for the IKFEM Festival (2024). "Fourteen Forty-Five (1445)" is the title of her debut album, referring to the distance in kilometers separating Ponta Delgada, her hometown, from Lisbon, where the record came to life.

22.09 EMERGENTE

This showcase is curated by the Emergente Tour of the Emergente Festival.

29.09 MARIANA CAMACHO + CARLOS RAPOSO

Mariana Camacho (Funchal, 1993) is a multifaceted artist moving across genres, driven by the urgency to explore all possible ways of making music as long as they bring fun and discovery. Since 2019 she has performed solo in the national independent circuit, fusing musical influences and world impressions without rules. Her research includes workshops on traditional root songs, exploring the voice as an expanded element that inhabits places and reflects landscapes. A lover of collective singing, she has passed through various choirs, directed CoLeGaS — LGBTI+ Choir of ILGA Portugal (2018–2025), is part of the vocal improvisation trio Guarda-Rios, collaborates as a singer and multi-instrumentalist, and participates in theater and dance projects like PULSAR - Companhia do Corpo.

Carlos Raposo toured Portugal in 2024 with the EP Trip to Innerlight and begins 2025 presenting his second EP, O Reino da Ilusão. This new work combines the drumming of traditional Portuguese snare drums and bass drums with the sweet tone of the campaniça guitar, intertwining with soundscapes of hypnotic, serene, beautiful, and melancholic electronics. A sonic journey making this "Kingdom of Illusion" an inevitable musical destination in 2025.

06.10 BERNARDO COUTO

Bernardo Couto, born December 19, 1979, began studying Portuguese guitar at age 13 with guitarist and composer Carlos Gonçalves. He graduated from the Conservatory of Music of the National Conservatory, completing the 7th grade in Portuguese Guitar and Musical Training. Years later, he began his professional career at the Fado house Mesa de Frades, since then developing a renowned career accompanying artists such as Raquel Tavares, Camané, Ana Moura, Cristina Branco, António Zambujo, and Rão Kyao. He is part of a duo with bandoneonist Martin Sued and the trio SUL, with Luís Figueiredo and Bernardo Moreira.
